blocks.text: Capital Amortization vs. Recurring Chemical Supply Line Items

When corporate facility managers conduct a supply premium legacy comparison for electrolyzed water and aqueous ozone cleaning cost, the primary accounting mistake is treating on-site electro-chemical activation (ECA) as a 100% substitute for bottled janitorial chemistry. In a standard US commercial office operating on a 5x-week daily weekday schedule (21.65 visits per month using the industry 4.33 weeks/month constant, with a 0.90 frequency multiplier), janitorial chemical concentrates—excluding paper towels, toilet tissue, hand soap, and can liners—typically account for just 2.5% to 4.5% of the gross monthly contract.

Conventional closed-loop dilution systems rely on concentrated neutral floor cleaners, quaternary or hydrogen-peroxide disinfectants, glass cleaners, and heavy-duty degreasers. On-site generation replaces the bulk of daily general-purpose spray-and-wipe and auto-scrubber fill liquids by passing cold tap water through either a diamond-coated electrode cell (creating stabilized aqueous ozone at 1.0 to 3.0 ppm) or a salt-brine membrane cell (producing hypochlorous acid at 50 to 200 ppm and sodium hydroxide degreaser). However, the financial equation hinges on water conditioning media, cartridge exchanges, and total square footage cleaned per night.

blocks.text: Why Legacy Concentrates Remain Surprisingly Competitive per Ready-to-Use Gallon

Vendor pitch decks for aqueous ozone systems frequently compare their cost per gallon against ready-to-use (RTU) trigger spray bottles purchased at retail, inflating the apparent chemical savings by 800% to 1,200%. Professional Building Service Contractors (BSCs) never buy RTU liquids for routine floor or surface maintenance. Instead, contractors utilize high-yield industrial concentrates that dilute at 1:128 (1 ounce per gallon) or 1:256 (0.5 ounces per gallon).

For example, when a janitorial crew maintains 15,000 sq ft of VCT/LVT vinyl flooring (which carries a 1.04 flooring labor multiplier for neutral-pH damp mopping and periodic buffing) or ceramic tile and grout (1.12 multiplier), a 5-gallon pail of Zep Neutral pH Industrial Floor Cleaner Concentrate diluted at 1:128 yields 640 ready-to-use gallons of no-rinse cleaning solution. That places the actual chemical cost per mop bucket or auto-scrubber tank at mere pennies. Consequently, displacing a 1:128 neutral floor concentrate with aqueous ozone takes thousands of dispensed gallons before the capital cost of the ozone generator, check valves, and desiccant dryers is recovered.

blocks.title: The 20,000 Sq Ft Payback Threshold
blocks.text: In multi-tenant or single-occupant offices smaller than 18,000 to 20,000 sq ft, installing a dedicated wall-mounted aqueous ozone or electrolyzed water generator rarely achieves pure chemical cost payback within a 36-month janitorial contract. Below that threshold, the primary justification is LEED v4.1 Operations and Maintenance (O+M) green cleaning credits, VOC elimination for sensitive occupants, and simplified OSHA Hazard Communication (HazCom) compliance rather than raw supply savings.
Hidden Operational Costs of On-Site Generation Systems

To build an accurate zero-based budget comparing on-site electro-chemical generation against conventional chemical procurement, facility directors must account for five recurring support expenses that frequently hide outside the base janitorial service agreement:

items: Air Dryer & Desiccant Cartridge Replacements: Aqueous ozone generators use corona discharge cells that require dry oxygen to maintain 1.5 to 3.0 ppm output. High humidity in unconditioned janitor closets degrades desiccant media every 3 to 6 months, adding $45 to $95 per cartridge exchange.

Water Softening & Deionization Pre-Filters: Hard municipal water (exceeding 7 grains per gallon) scales electrolytic plates and fouls ozone venturi injectors. Sites in hard-water corridors must budget $120 to $250 annually for scale-inhibiting filter cartridges.

Potency Half-Life & Re-Fill Labor: Stabilized aqueous ozone reverts to plain water and oxygen within 4 to 24 hours in a trigger bottle, while unbuffered hypochlorous acid loses active free available chlorine over 14 to 30 days. Night crews must dump and refill spray bottles at the start of every shift, adding 8 to 12 minutes of labor per janitor per week ($35–$65/hour standard labor rate).

Plumbing Backflow Prevention & Electrical Drops: Installing a wall-mounted unit in a leased corporate suite mop closet requires a dedicated 120V GFCI receptacle and an ASSE-approved reduced-pressure backflow preventer, costing $350 to $750 in initial facilities trade labor.

ORP & Free Chlorine Verification Strips: Quality assurance requires supervisors to dip test strips weekly to confirm Oxidation-Reduction Potential (ORP >= 750 mV) or active ppm levels, adding $15 to $25 per month in QA consumables.

blocks.text: Where Hybrid Conventional Chemistry Is Still Required by Scope

Even in flagship green corporate headquarters committed to chemical-free daily wiping, aqueous ozone and electrolyzed water cannot legally or physically perform every task in a commercial janitorial scope of work. When comparing total supply budgets, procurement officers must preserve a dedicated line item for specialized conventional products across three high-friction zones:

items.name: High-Touch Outbreak & Bloodborne Pathogen Disinfection
items.text: Aqueous ozone is regulated by the EPA as a pesticide device (carrying an EPA Establishment Number) rather than an EPA List N registered liquid chemical disinfectant. Furthermore, its rapid half-life makes it unsuitable for daytime tenant self-service. Facilities routinely stage CloroxPro Clorox Disinfecting Wipes Commercial Bucket (700-Count) units—featuring an EPA List N bleach-free formula in a refillable 700-wipe dispenser—at reception desks, shared hot-desking pods, and conference tables for immediate viral dwell-time compliance.

items.name: Breakroom Polymerized Grease & Loading Dock Soils
items.text: Aqueous ozone excels at oxidizing light organic films and deodorizing porous grout, but it lacks the surfactants required to emulsify baked-on microwave grease, coffee oils, or petroleum tracks at warehouse entries. Night crews cleaning breakrooms ($12–$25 per visit add-on) rely on a concentrated biodegradable surfactant such as Simple Green Pro HD Heavy-Duty Cleaner & Degreaser (1-Gallon), which uses a phosphate-free, non-corrosive formula to cut heavy oils without damaging stainless steel appliances.

items.name: Finished VCT & Sealed Stone Preservation
items.text: Repeated application of unbuffered salt-brine electrolyzed water can leave microscopic sodium chloride crystal residue on dark luxury vinyl tile (LVT) or dull high-gloss acrylic floor finishes over time. Contractors running quarterly deep floor programs ($0.03–$0.06/sq ft/month amortized) pair daily dust mopping with Zep Neutral pH Industrial Floor Cleaner Concentrate (5-Gallon Pail) at a 1:128 dilution ratio to guarantee zero alkaline blush on finished hard floors.

blocks.text: Labor Productivity Impact: ISSA 3,500 Sq Ft/Hr Benchmarks

Because labor consumes 75% to 82% of a commercial cleaning invoice, a 3% shift in cleaner productivity outweighs a 25% swing in chemical supply cost. Using the ISSA benchmark of 3,500 sq ft per hour for standard office maintenance at $35 to $65 per billable labor hour, on-site generation delivers its strongest financial return not by saving chemical dollars, but by reducing rework and multi-step surface rinsing.

Conventional all-purpose cleaners and quaternary disinfectants contain surfactants that build up a tacky microscopic film on interior glass partitions ($15–$35 per visit add-on), laminate desks, and ceramic restroom fixtures ($15–$30 per restroom per visit) if overdosed by poorly trained workers. Aqueous ozone leaves zero surfactant residue when wiped with high-GSM microfiber, allowing a single technician to clean glass sidelights, stainless elevator doors, and laminate worktables from one trigger bottle without switching between blue glass spray and green multi-surface spray. In facilities above 25,000 sq ft, shaving 15 minutes per night off chemical bottle swapping and streak remediation saves $190 to $350 per month in direct labor—often exceeding the entire chemical concentrate savings.

blocks.title: Portable Spray Bottle Generators vs. Plumbed Wall Units
blocks.text: If your office occupies 3,000 to 10,000 sq ft and only requires 1x/week (4.33 visits/mo, 1.08 multiplier) or 2x/week (8.66 visits/mo, 1.00 multiplier) service, forbid your contractor from billing a plumbed wall-unit lease. Instead, specify a portable rechargeable electrolytic spray bottle or batch pitcher system ($180–$350 one-time hardware outlay), which eliminates plumbing costs and achieves ROI in under 7 months.

faqs.q: How much should an aqueous ozone or electrolyzed water program add to a monthly office cleaning bid?
faqs.a: In commercial offices above 20,000 sq ft cleaned 5x per week (21.65 visits/month), an on-site aqueous ozone or electrolyzed water program should add $0.00 to your net per-square-foot rate ($0.05–$0.12/sq ft), because the contractor's reduced spend on daily multi-purpose and glass concentrates offsets the $115–$210 monthly equipment and filter amortization. In smaller suites under 10,000 sq ft ($0.09–$0.15/sq ft base rate), expect a modest net supply premium of $45 to $85 per month unless the vendor uses portable batch generators across multiple client accounts.

faqs.q: Does switching to electrolyzed water eliminate OSHA HazCom and SDS binder requirements?
faqs.a: It dramatically reduces OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 Hazard Communication exposure for daily spray-and-wipe tasks—often allowing cleaners to work without chemical splash goggles or nitrile gloves during general dusting and damp mopping—and removes the need for plumbed eyewash stations required by corrosive concentrated acid/alkaline dispensers. However, your janitor closet must still maintain a compliant Safety Data Sheet (SDS) binder for mandatory backup products like EPA List N hospital disinfectants, heavy-duty breakroom degreasers, and VCT floor strippers.

faqs.q: Can aqueous ozone completely replace EPA List N disinfectants for OSHA bloodborne pathogen compliance?
faqs.a: No. Under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030), any spill involving blood or potentially infectious bodily fluids must be decontaminated using an EPA-registered tuberculocidal or HIV/HBV-effective liquid disinfectant with a verified wet contact dwell time, or a fresh sodium hypochlorite bleach dilution. Aqueous ozone generators are regulated as EPA pesticide devices rather than registered liquid chemicals, so contractors must still stock EPA List N disinfectant wipes or concentrates in the closet.

faqs.q: Who pays for replacement electrode cells and water filtration cartridges in a janitorial contract?
faqs.a: In a turnkey full-service janitorial contract, the Building Service Contractor should own or lease the generator and absorb all desiccant dryer, deionization filter, and electrode cell replacements inside their base overhead. If the property management firm purchases the wall-mounted unit directly as a building capital improvement, ensure the service level agreement (SLA) assigns weekly ORP strip testing to the cleaning crew while keeping annual filter kit replacements ($150–$350/year) in the facility engineering budget.
